submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires when the current token continues the ongoing constituent, i.e. it is directly licensed by the immediately preceding token (determiner/adjective/quantifier/preposition/auxiliary-negation selecting a noun or verb, a stem selecting its completion, an identifier selecting its operator or argument in code), and it stays near zero on constituent onsets such as sentence-initial words, clause-linking conjunctions and nouns starting a new subject. Its output direction promotes no coherent token set (Jacobian kurtosis ~3.4, incoherent promoted list), so it is a retrospective local-continuation detector, not a next-token predictor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Field log week fourteen, coastal survey team. Monday we catalogued tide pools near the northern jetty and recorded gull counts at dawn. Tuesday the radio failed so we relayed messages by hand between the ridge station and the boathouse. Wednesday we repaired the winch, sorted rope coils, and calibrated the depth sounder against the harbour chart. Thursday brought fog that hid the cliffs until noon, then a clear afternoon we used to photograph lichen plots on the granite slabs. Friday we interviewed the ferry crew about winter swells, copied their annotations onto our charts, and restocked kerosene, rice, dried apricots, nails, canvas patches, and batteries. Saturday the generator coughed and died, so we worked by lantern and logged salinity readings every hour through the night. Sunday we rested, mended nets, boiled seawater for salt samples, and wrote letters to the mainland office. Week fifteen opened with gales that pinned us in the hut while rain hammered the shutters and the barometer kept falling. When the wind eased we hiked the cliff path, counted seal pups on the ledges, and marked two fresh rockfalls on the survey map. The botanist pressed fern specimens between newspaper sheets and labelled each with date, altitude, and exposure. The engineer rebuilt the tripod leg from driftwood and tested it with the heavy theodolite on the shingle spit. We traded potatoes with the lighthouse keeper for lamp oil and heard news of a stranded trawler near the outer reef. Evening classes covered knot tying, first aid for hypothermia, signal flags, chart symbols, and tide arithmetic for new volunteers. Supplies ran low again, so we rationed coffee, patched the tent seams, and fished for mackerel off the stone pier. A pod of dolphins crossed the bay at sunset while gulls trailed the returning boats into the harbour mouth. Night watches recorded meteor counts, wind shifts, cloud cover, and the phosphorescence trailing the mooring buoy. On the final morning we packed the crates, checked the manifests, paid the boatman, and walked the headland trail where seabirds nested on narrow shelves, until finally we sighted the ancient lighthouse
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context cross-genre holdout placing a determiner-adjective-noun continuation hundreds of tokens deep in a field log, predicts active on the final noun.
